themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints in CD 302 spiked to 10 this week versus 0.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,233% increase (z-score: 11.16)—signaling a potential new public safety crisis in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights requiring urgent investigation into whether this reflects actual activity escalation or increased reporting.
evidence: 10 drug activity complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 per week 8-week baseline
Z-score of 11.16 indicates extreme statistical anomaly (well above 2.0 threshold)
No prior Reddit discussions or local news mentions suggest this may be newly emerging or newly visible
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD precinct commanders and community residents about what's driving the spike—new distribution network, open-air market, or increased resident reporting?
Map complaint locations to identify geographic hotspots within Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights and examine whether complaints cluster near transit hubs or residential areas

themes_detail.label: Water System Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints surged to 33 this week, up 181% from an 11.8 per-week baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.04), suggesting widespread plumbing infrastructure failures or service disruptions affecting residents across CD 302.
evidence: 33 water system complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.8 per week 8-week baseline
Z-score of 4.04 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Heat/hot water complaints remain chronically high (605 total over 90 days), suggesting winter-season infrastructure strain compounded by acute water system failures
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine if a main break, hydrant issue, or service interruption occurred this week; cross-reference with ULURP applications for 395 Flatbush Ave and Columbia Heights rezoning for subsurface construction
Interview affected residents and building owners about water outages, discoloration, or pressure loss; investigate whether older housing stock in Brooklyn Heights is disproportionately impacted

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Wave
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints jumped to 18 this week, up 414% from a 3.5 per-week baseline (z-score: 4.77), indicating concentrated unauthorized tree removal or destruction, possibly connected to development activity or seasonal maintenance practices.
evidence: 18 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.5 per week 8-week baseline
Z-score of 4.77 indicates highly significant statistical spike
1,226 building permits filed in last 90 days (873 alterations) may correlate with contractors damaging street trees during renovation work
reporting_angles: Request Parks Department enforcement records for CD 302 this week; investigate whether contractors on active alteration projects are violating tree protection rules
Interview Parks enforcement and identify whether complaints are concentrated in areas of active ULURP applications (395 Flatbush Ave Ext., Columbia Heights rezoning)

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints rose to 41 this week, up 133% from a 17.6 per-week baseline (z-score: 3.48), reflecting potential rodent, waste management, or cleanliness failures across the district that may endanger public health.
evidence: 41 unsanitary condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 17.6 per week 8-week baseline
Converges with water system spike (33 complaints) and street condition issues (673 total over 90 days), suggesting systemic neighborhood cleanliness deterioration
reporting_angles: Obtain DSNY/Sanitation Department records for increased complaints about trash accumulation, missed pickups, or street filth this week in specific blocks

Interview residents and local business owners about whether rodent sightings, pest complaints, or odors coincide with the spike; investigate whether water system failures are creating pooling/sewage issues

themes_detail.label: Building Code & Habitability Failures
themes_detail.summary: Flooring/stairs complaints spiked to 12 this week (up 357% from 2.6 baseline, z-score: 4.1) and appliance complaints jumped to 6 last week (up 336%, z-score: 6.65), alongside heat/hot water's chronic high volume (605 over 90 days), signaling accelerating habitability code violations in residential units.
evidence: Flooring/stairs: 12 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 per week baseline (357% increase, z-score 4.1)
Appliance issues: 6 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 per week baseline (336% increase, z-score 6.65)
Heat/hot water remains persistently elevated at 605 total complaints over 90 days, indicating seasonal winter habitability crisis
reporting_angles: File FOIL request for HPD inspection and violation data for CD 302 this week/month; identify landlords with repeat habitability violations and cross-reference against tenant complaints

Interview tenants in older buildings (particularly in Brooklyn Heights) about inadequate heat, broken appliances, and structural hazards; investigate whether landlords are deferring maintenance or failing to comply with repair orders
